items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said Dizzy went to him and said, “What you did for me, can you do for musicians?” So Frank loved to do that.

ctx.x: Well, it’s all very beautiful. These were people who just love jazz, and they were all involved with the museum. A few things had happened, and the space was taken away, and they really didn’t know what to do. They gave everything to the Schomberg. But then they said, “Why don’t we become an organization to keep jazz alive and to archive it, to promote it?” I think for a couple of years, it sort of went along like that. I know they did an event at Town Hall which helped them raise some money. And then, Jamil…

items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: the Englewood Hospital in Jersey was taking musicians for free because of a relationship with Dizzy Gillespie

ctx.x: Well you’ve certainly made good on your passion and your humanity. And am I correct that you’re still doing it in your new location?

Yes. Yeah. The foundation, you know I basically have turned into – within two years we were national. I was helping musicians not just in New York but finding out about someone in another state, finding out they needed a doctor, they had no health insurance, finding out who the specialist was in that state and ask them would you just take on this one musician for free, could you please. And we’d get this doctors’ network going and our blessed saints, the Englewood Hospital in Jersey was taking musicians for free…

generated 70 million dollars later, and helping about 8,000 cases a year, and we would help. Like a case could be sometimes two or three for one musician because there was always such a need. There was the short term need of like getting the rent paid so they don’t get evicted and lose their rent-controlled apartment, and then there was the long term need, finding out they needed to have work in order to keep paying the rent. So I had developed the Jazz in the Schools program which ended up across the country…
